draft.title: Hypothetical Checklist for Offline Local LLM Testing (Generation & Network)
draft.body: This post outlines a hypothetical checklist for testing local LLMs offline, based on a synthetic experimental brief. The core idea is to verify a model's functionality without an internet connection. The proposed steps focus on two key areas: ensuring the model can still generate text and confirming it makes no unintended network requests. Fact F1 states that models can be downloaded beforehand, which is a prerequisite for any offline testing. Fact F2 specifies that the offline verification must encompass both text generation and monitoring for network activity. It's crucial to remember, as per Fact F3, that no actual offline test has been performed in this scenario; this is purely a planning exercise. The objective is to establish a structured approach for future hypothetical evaluations. We aim to confirm that a downloaded model operates entirely locally as expected. Further discussion on refining these hypothetical steps would be welcome.

draft.title: Planning a Hypothetical Offline Test for Local LLMs: Generation & Network Monitoring
draft.body: This is a guide for a hypothetical experiment to test local LLMs in an offline environment. The scenario, based on synthetic input, allows for pre-downloading models (F1). The primary goal is to validate that a model operates entirely without network access after disconnection. The proposed test procedure involves two main components: first, verifying the model's ability to generate coherent text, and second, actively monitoring for any network requests initiated by the model or its associated processes. This rigorous check ensures true offline operation. Importantly, this entire process is a hypothetical exercise as detailed in Fact F3; no actual offline tests have been conducted. The intention is to create a robust framework for evaluating offline LLM capabilities. We are interested in feedback on the completeness of this hypothetical testing plan, particularly regarding the generation and network monitoring aspects.

Clearly state that this is a hypothetical scenario and no real tests have occurred. Seek community input on the effectiveness of this planned testing approach.
